step2.title: Chunking Settings
step2.subtitle: Adjust how documents are split into chunks. Default values work well for most cases.
step2.modeAutomaticDesc: The system automatically applies optimal chunking strategy based on document type
step2.removeextraspacesTooltip: Compresses multiple consecutive newlines into two, and multiple spaces/tabs into one. Helps clean up poorly formatted documents.
step2.removeurlsemailsTooltip: Removes email addresses and URLs from the text. Markdown image URLs are preserved. Useful when URLs/emails are noise, but disable if they contain important information.
step2.maxTokensTooltip: Maximum number of tokens per chunk. Smaller chunks (300-500) provide more precise retrieval but may lose context. Larger chunks (800-1000) preserve more context but may reduce precision.
step2.chunkOverlapTooltip: Number of overlapping tokens between adjacent chunks. Overlap helps preserve context at chunk boundaries. Recommended: 10-20% of max chunk size.
step2.helpOverview: Documents are split into chunks through a 2-stage process:
step2.helpStage1Desc: First, the text is split using your chosen delimiter (e.g., newline). Each piece is checked against the max chunk size.
step2.helpStage2Desc: If any piece exceeds the max chunk size, it's further split using fallback separators in order:
step2.helpMerge: Small pieces are then merged back together up to the max chunk size, with overlap between adjacent chunks to preserve context.
step2.helpExampleSettings: Settings: Delimiter='\n', Max Size=50 chars, Overlap=10 chars
step2.helpExampleOriginalText:
Hi.
This is a very long sentence that exceeds the limit. It needs to be split further.
Bye.
step2.helpExampleStep1Result:
Piece 1: "Hi." (3 chars) ✓
Piece 2: "This is a very long sentence..." (73 chars) ✗ exceeds 50!
Piece 3: "Bye." (4 chars) ✓
step2.helpExampleStep2: Step 2 - Re-split oversized piece by '. ' (fallback separator):
step2.helpExampleStep2Result:
Piece 2a: "This is a very long sentence that exceeds the limit." (52 chars)
Piece 2b: "It needs to be split further." (30 chars)
→ Piece 2a still over 50, but no more '. ' to split, so kept as-is
step2.helpExampleStep3: Step 3 - Merge small pieces into chunks (max 50 chars):
step2.helpExampleStep3Result:
"Hi." (3) → too small alone, but next piece is too big
→ Chunk 1: "Hi." (3 chars)
→ Chunk 2: "This is a very long sentence that exceeds the limit." (52 chars)
→ Chunk 3: "It needs to be split further." + "Bye." = 34 chars
step2.helpExampleStep4: Step 4 - Apply overlap (10 chars) between chunks:
step2.helpExampleStep4Result:
Chunk 1: "Hi."
Chunk 2: "Hi. This is a very long sentence that exceeds the limit."
     ↑↑↑ (overlap from chunk 1)
Chunk 3: "the limit. It needs to be split further. Bye."
     ↑↑↑↑↑↑↑↑↑↑ (overlap from chunk 2)
step2.helpExampleFinal: Final result: 3 chunks with overlapping context preserved
